answers.text: Build the condo tower to budget (within reasonable range) and sell the condos at expected pricing (within range discussed).

If things don't go to plan, there are a few options. 
The units can always be rented if they do not sell.
The units can be sold for less and investors will receive a smaller return.
Limited partners can sell their shares if they need to liquidate.
We can refinance the building and change to rentals. The refinance could potentially return all of the investors investment and provide some cash flow.

As units sell the waterfall is as follows:
Repay debt (Anticipated to be around $100M)
Repay Pref Equity ($5.0M)
Repay LP investment ($18M)
Pay LP pref (12% accrued, paid from deal profit)
Pay LP profit (remaining after the pref above)
Uncertain what fee structure this is referring to

The construction loan will be around 7.15% over the 30 day SOFR rate which today puts it just over 10%. We will also be buying a cap which means that the rate won't go over the max rate we set which will most likely be 11%. So in layman's terms, the most the rate can go is 11% and if rates begin to recede next year (which we believe they will), we will benefit from a lower rate than the current one.
This is not normal but if there is an urgent need, as we have before, we will consider buying the investment back at Par value.

Standard "bad boy carveouts"  We promise to be good boys. This means that we have to comply with the loan terms. Standard loan terms include completion guarantee, carry guarantee, environmental indemnification, etc. As long as we build it and pay our interest payments, we won't have a problem.
Absolute worst case, while highly unlikely, would be a loss of investment. We feel we've mitigated many of the risks as discussed.
We provide quarterly updates that disclose spent to date and sales to date and any other pertinent information.
